      <title>Norwegian ber 5000 kundar sperre bankkortet etter datainnbrot</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/norwegian-ber-5000-kundar-sperre-bankkortet-etter-datainnbrot-1.18085456</link>
      <description>Norwegian har teke kontakt med rundt 5000 kundar og bede dei sperre bankkorta sine etter at ein leverandør til nettsidene deira er utsett for datainnbrot, melder NTB.
Ein skadeleg kode blei lagt inn på nettsidene til Norwegian, som gjorde at kortdetaljar som blei brukt på nettsida kan ha vore synlege i ein kortare periode måndag.
Selskapet oppdaga datainnbrotet onsdag.
Hendinga er rapportert til Datatilsynet.
I førre veke blei det kjent at 144.000 passasjerar hos Norwegian og Widerøe blei lekka i forbindelse med eit datainnbrot hos ein spansk IT-leverandør.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Israel med ny offensiv – tre drept</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/israel-med-ny-offensiv-_-tre-drept-1.18084431</link>
      <description>Israels hær sier den har innledet en operasjon i Hamas-kontrollerte områder i Gaza
Israel har innledet en militæroperasjon i det sentrale Gaza vest for den såkalte gule linjen, som har skilt Hamas-kontrollerte og israelsk-kontrollerte områder siden våpenhvilen trådte i kraft i fjor. Det opplyser militæret til AFP.
Vitner sier at israelske stridsvogner rullet inn på hovedveien Salahudeen, vest for den såkalte gule linjen som markerer grensen for de to tredjedelene av Gazastripen som fortsatt er under israelsk kontroll.
Den såkalte gule linjen ble etablert etter våpenhvilen i oktober 2025 og skiller israelskkontrollerte og palestinske soner i Gazastripen. Israelske styrker har gradvis flyttet den gule linjen og utvidet området under direkte militær kontroll i Gaza.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/stor-oslo/skarstein_-_-heldigvis-er-det-lov-a-tenke-seg-om-1.18082145</link>
      <description>Tidligere idrettsutøver Birgit Skarstein sier hun er klar til å bidra dersom hun blir ordførerkandidat for Arbeiderpartiet.
Oslo Aps nominasjonskomité samlet seg fredag kveld om den tidligere parautøveren som ordførerkandidat ved kommunevalget neste høst.
Skarstein sa først nei til plassen, men endret senere mening.
– Da nominasjonskomiteen ringte tre uker senere, hadde vi fått områdd oss, og jeg kjente at jeg var veldig motivert. Heldigvis er det lov å tenke seg om, skriver hun i et innlegg på Facebook.
Den endelige avgjørelsen skal tas på nominasjonsmøtet i Samfunnssalen over Sentrum Scene 22. november.</description>

A British Columbia First Nation says lives and food security are at risk after two recent rail accidents on the 103-year-old track along the Skeena River.

]]>

A British Columbia First Nation says lives and food security are at risk after two recent rail accidents on the 103-year-old track along the Skeena River.

The Gitxsan Huwilp Government says in a statement that the latest derailment has reignited its call for the “immediate stop to all train hauling” in its traditional territories and fishing waterways, calling the practice dangerous.

Several railcars jumped the tracks on Tuesday, spilling diesel and sending some cars loaded with forest products into the Skeena River about 15 kilometres west of Terrace. 

CN Rail announced the track had been repaired and train traffic resumed on Thursday, while the two crew members who were injured in the derailment have been released from hospital.

The company says environmental protection measures are in place in the river and specialized environmental response teams remain at the site, working to contain and recover spilled diesel fuel and removing derailed equipment.

The First Nation says it is the second such incident in eight months, after a mudslide derailed grain cars travelling along the river south of Prince Rupert in March, resulting in a spill of nearly 8,000 litres of diesel.

Hereditary chief Toby Howard says the latest accident demonstrates the continuing risks posed by freight transportation through Gitxsan territory.

“A 103-year-old track has created dangerous conditions for the rail system in our territory,” he says in the statement. 

CN Rail did not immediately respond to a request for a response to the nation’s calls to halt train hauling in the territory.

Howard says the nation’s hereditary chiefs have offered the provincial government assistance in identifying “the areas of most vulnerability on the line” but the Transportation Ministry has dismissed the offer.

“The hauling of any materials — dangerous, human or otherwise — must stop immediately until CN Rail can guarantee the rail line is safe,” he says.

The derailment is also “well within the reach of ocean tides, jeopardizing an entire ecosystem,” the First Nation statement says.

“We must ensure that every inch of the railway from Burns Lake to Prince Rupert is inspected, otherwise our Gitxsan people are not safe,” Howards says.

CN Rail said it appears a rock slide caused Tuesday’s derailment, which involved two locomotives and five railcars.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 19, 2026.

]]> 1362668 Old Navy and Gap retailers under investigation for alleged misleading marketing practices https://cheknews.ca/old-navy-and-gap-retailers-under-investigation-for-alleged-misleading-marketing-practices-1362648/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 20:31:38 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362648

The Competition Bureau is investigating retailers Old Navy and Gap for alleged "false or misleading marketing practices."

The post Old Navy and Gap retailers under investigation for alleged misleading marketing practices appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The Competition Bureau is investigating retailers Old Navy and Gap for alleged “false or misleading marketing practices.”

Wednesday, the bureau said it obtained a court order to investigate “whether specific marketing practices used by Old Navy and Gap raise concerns under the deceptive marketing provisions of the Competition Act,” according to a news release.

It’s specifically examining false advertising of sales and discounts, false urgency marketing such as limited-time offers, falsely advertising low inventory, such as “Selling Fast” or “Only a Few Left,” as well as inflating the number of people viewing the product or false advertising of past prices or discounts, like “Price Drop” or “Best Deal in 30 Days.”

To date, the bureau says “there has been no finding of wrongdoing at this time.”

The investigation sparked after the bureau saw a surge in complaints of inflated prices in 2025. In response to the complaints, it issued a warning, reminding businesses of what advertising tactics are considered illegal under the Competition Act.

Both Old Navy and Gap fall under the parent company Gap Inc., but advertise exclusively to their respective brands, selling through brick-and-mortar stores and online e-commerce websites.

The investigation comes a week away from one of the biggest shopping seasons in North America, Black Friday. In 2024, the Bureau issued a shoppers beware alert, warning consumers of fake urgency cues and to report any false or misleading claims.

“Don’t be pressured by fake urgency cues in the marketplace,” it states.

To determine whether the urgency pressure is fake or real, the bureau says to watch for patterns and question the claims:

  • Does the business frequently repeat or renew a promotion after the deadline?
  • Does the business frequently make low stock claims but items continue to be in stock over time?
  • Does the countdown timer run out or reset and the deal is still available?
  • If other shoppers are currently looking at the product, does the available inventory decline over time?

CHEK has reached out to Gap Inc. for a comment but has not received a response at this time.

The post Old Navy and Gap retailers under investigation for alleged misleading marketing practices appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A British Columbia Supreme Court judge has ordered that a decision to label a mine in northwestern B.C. as “substantially started” be sent back to the provincial government and that it must have “deep consultation” with the territory’s First Nation.

The province’s assessment officer ruled in 2024 that Seabridge Gold’s KSM Project, a proposed copper, gold and silver mine 65 kilometres northwest of Stewart, B.C., had substantially started, meaning it had made enough progress to retain its environmental approval.

Justice Emily Burke originally ruled in June that the province had not satisfied its duty to consult with the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation regarding the substantial start decision, but both sides returned to her courtroom asking for clarity on how to interpret the ruling. 

In the latest decision, Burke says the substantial start determination is quashed and that the province must give the nation 90 days’ notice to present written submissions addressing the question of whether the project was substantially started.

The nation says in a statement on Thursday that following the initial ruling in June, Seabridge issued a news release incorrectly announcing that the court found the substantial start determination reasonable.

Chief Darlene Simpson says the nation is not against responsible resource development but is concerned about a 52-storey-deep, nine-kilometre-long “toxic waste dump that uses a wet tailings approach” that has been found unsafe elsewhere.

“If the province grants the (substantial start determination) to this project, our nation will have to live with that looming disaster on our territory for hundreds of years, because that poison can’t be moved and is of great risk of breaching containment over time,” she says in a statement issued Thursday.

“With yesterday’s court decision, we hope the province finally understands it has to engage seriously with our concerns about such momentous effects on our territory.”

]]> 1362634 Menopause drug made in Canada won’t be available to Canadians, but still sold in U.S. https://cheknews.ca/menopause-drug-made-in-canada-wont-be-available-to-canadians-but-still-sold-in-u-s-1362637/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 19:35:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362637

Canadian women will no longer have access to a menopause drug that is made in Canada, even though the drugmaker plans to continue producing it for patients in the United States.

The post Menopause drug made in Canada won’t be available to Canadians, but still sold in U.S. appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Canadian women will no longer have access to a menopause drug that is made in Canada, even though the drugmaker plans to continue producing it for patients in the United States.

Pfizer has discontinued Premarin estrogen tablets and vaginal cream, used for decades to treat menopausal and post-menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal burning and dryness, abnormal uterine bleeding, and osteoporosis prevention.

The active ingredient, conjugated equine estrogen, comes from pregnant mares’ urine collected at 12 family-owned ranches in Manitoba and Saskatchewan since the early 1940s.

Pfizer discontinued the vaginal cream for Canadians in early November citing “business reasons.” The company says the tablet will be off the market starting next year in June.

Meanwhile, ranchers in the prairies will continue to collect the raw ingredients, brought to a manufacturing facility in Brandon, Man., where estrogen is extracted, says Norman Luba, executive director of the region’s equine ranching association.

Pfizer Canada’s senior communications manager Sophie Morin said the products have become “commercially unsustainable” for the drugmaker to keep supplying to Canadians.

The decision was not “driven solely by the pricing conditions for Premarin in Canada,” Morin said, also citing manufacturing and supply costs, the pricing and reimbursement environment, and the ability to maintain sustainable supply over the longer term.

Dr. Jennifer Gunter, a gynecologist from Manitoba based in the United States, wrote on her Substack that the price of a tube of Premarin cream in Canada is about C$50, while the same tube in the U.S. sells for approximately US$400 to $500.

Gunter urged Canadians to be concerned about Pfizer’s decision, listing several reasons, including that limiting medication is never good for women. She also says Premarin has been shown to reduce the risk of breast cancer, and it is covered by provincial drug plans.

“This isn’t just about Premarin. Every Canadian who cares about access to medications needs to be engaged and speak up,” Gunter wrote.

Menopause expert Dr. Michelle Jacobson said it feels wrong that she won’t be able to prescribe Premarin to her patients, despite the fact that this is a drug that comes from Canada.

“Globally, it is, the supply chain starts in Canada, and yet, for reasons that are not completely transparent, Canadians are now not going to be able to access this homegrown raw material,” Jacobson said.

In response to concerns from physicians and patients, Marin said Pfizer understands, and recognizes “changes in the availability of a medicine can be difficult for those who rely on it.”

Health Canada says it is assessing the impact of the discontinuation and collaborating with clinical and pharmacy stakeholders to support continuity of care. The regulator also put out a notice on Thursday about a shortage of Premarin Intravenous for abnormal uterine bleeding associated with hormonal imbalance, expected to last from December to May due to a manufacturing disruption.

PUBLIC HEALTH PLANS AND PREMARIN CREAM

Some provincial public health plans, for instance Ontario, covered Pfizer’s Premarin cream but not the alternative cream on the market.

Lily Barnes, a spokesperson for the ministry of health in Ontario, says there are other estrogen drug products covered by the province’s drug benefits, such as a vaginal ring, tablet and insert.

However, Jacobson says the active ingredients are different in those products. She also says the vaginal cream can be better for certain conditions, such as dryness.

Meanwhile, Alberta’s ministry of health says that as a result of Pfizer’s move it is adding Estragyn vaginal cream, made by Searchlight Pharma, to the province’s drug benefit list to ensure women still have access.

A spokesperson said it is a temporary measure the ministry plans to make permanent. Quebec and Manitoba’s provincial drug benefits already cover the alternative.

PRODUCTION SEASON UNDERWAY ON RANCHES

Luba, executive director of the North American Equine Ranching Information Council, said the Canadian ranchers are proud of what they do, and while there might be “some disappointment,” it’s ultimately the company’s decision.

He said the ranchers are busy as their production season gets underway this week.

That means bringing horses into the barn, collecting their urine, and storing it in a steel bulk tank until a truck comes to pick it up, similar to a dairy cow production.

“I’ve often said it’s a great partnership between women’s health care and rural Canadian agriculture,” Luba said.

It’s become something of a familiar sight in Greater Victoria, a massive elephant seal hauling itself onto land to moult.

Now, a new seal has taken up residence at Cutbert Holmes Park in Saanich, and while he may not be garnering the same attention as former local star Emerson the elephant seal, Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) is still asking onlookers to stay away.

The elephant seal popped up at the park earlier this week, and since then DFO staff have set up a fence around the animal to make sure trail users keep their distance from the seal as it completes its annual moult.

A moult involves an elephant seal coming ashore for roughly a month, where it sheds its fur and underlying skin.

The process is exhausting and can even be painful.

“The seal is largely confined to land during the moulting process and spends most of its time dozing and lazily flipping sand onto itself to stay cool,” said DFO in a statement Thursday. “It doesn’t eat and may lose up to 25% of its body weight.”

Besides people, the DFO is asking that pets be kept away from the seal, as it can be disturbed it and spread diseases like Leptospirosis and Seal Pox.

The federal organization notes that disturbing marine mammals – including feeding, interacting or moving a marine mammal – can result in fines up to $100,000.

“Elephant seals are wild animals, and while they may look slow and harmless, they are capable of moving very quickly and could be dangerous if they feel threatened,” said the DFO.

Remembering a local legend

In 2024, a wily elephant seal dubbed “Emerson” by the community made headlines for his repeated visits to Greater Victoria.

The juvenile elephant seal, which weighed about 500 pounds, came to Saanich and Victoria in the spring and had to be relocated twice for things like blocking traffic.

The first time, in April 2024, he was relocated from Saanich to the Barkley Sound area of Vancouver Island about 150 kilometres away, but remarkably returned to Victoria after roughly a week.

He was then relocated again on May 9, 2024, after setting himself up in the Victoria Yacht Club area, a location that the DFO felt was unsafe for himself and motorists.

He hasn’t been heard from since then, and on Thursday the DFO confirmed the elephant seal at Cutbert Holmes Park was not Emerson.

“So far this year, DFO has not received any news about Emerson’s whereabouts,” said the organization.

The DFO says it will continue to monitor the seal currently at Cutbert Holmes Park, and adds that anyone who sees someone harassing a marine mammal can contact Fisheries and Oceans Canada at 1-800-465-4336 or by email at DFO.ORR-ONS.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca.

Port Alberni’s fire chief says crews spent nearly two hours on the defensive attack, chasing heavy flames from the exterior of a structure fire before they were able to chainsaw their way inside and continue battling the blaze.

Around 4:30 a.m. Thursday, crews from multiple departments responded to a structure fire with heavy flames at Melrose Street and 1st Avenue, says Chief Mike Owens of PAFD.

“There were flames shooting at least 15 feet above the roofline of the structure,” Owens tells CHEK, adding, “Our initial priorities were to prevent fire spread to an adjacent structure to the north of that building.”

Crews were able to contain the flames to the building of origin, with help from PAFD’s mutual aid partners, Cherry Creek and Beaver Creek volunteer fire departments.

In total, 15 firefighters were on scene battling the heavy flames shooting from the building. According to Owens, the building had been vacant for quite some time and was boarded up.

“With the volume of fire and coupled with that information, we took a defensive approach,” he says, spending roughly two hours attacking defensively from the exterior.

“We were able to knock the fire down, but it took a couple hours on scene chasing it to keep it contained,” he said.

Vacant building slated for demolition

By 6:30 a.m., crews moved from initial defensive attack to demobilization inside the building.

Crews had to use chainsaws to gain entry to the building, and once inside they approached cautiously as they did not know what stage of demolition the building was in.

“As it was subject to a demolition permit that was already taken out by the owner, the building itself was already boarded up, so that presented some access challenges initially. So we needed to use forcible entry tools,” says Owens.

No one was injured and the damage was contained to the building.

“The structure still stands, but there is some considerable fire damage to the structure,” he says.

According to BC Assessment, the building was valued at $1,000 before the fire.

Built in 1935, it’s listed as a vacant, one-storey, 413-square-foot building that sits on less than two acres of land, currently assessed at $181,000.

As for whether there had been demolition tools or signs of recent activity inside, Owens said it was too early to know.

The cause of the fire is still under investigation, with investigators still on site at around 10:30 a.m.

“We understand that there has been some activity recently as part of the demolition process but at this point, again, investigators are working to determine what the cause of fire was. Nothing is sticking out,” said Owens.

Traffic was initially diverted away from the closed portion of 1st Avenue on Harbour Road and Melrose Street, but has since reopened.

British Columbia’s Environmental Assessment Office has paused its review of the Massey Tunnel replacement project at the request of the province, saying it “understands the rationale” related to the transition to a new government.

A letter posted to the project page on the office’s website shows the Transportation Ministry and the Transportation Investment Corporation asked for the pause given the interregnum period after the B.C. Conservatives toppled the NDP government in the Oct. 24 snap election.

The letter dated Nov. 16 says it would be appropriate to allow the incoming government — which is to be sworn in Friday — to establish its priorities and provide further direction on the project, where construction is already underway.

The Environmental Assessment Office responded the next day pausing its review, but asking the corporation to remain ready to support a resumption of the process should the new government decide to seek a certificate for the existing project.

Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson promised during his campaign to scrap the $8.5-billion tunnel in favour of a bridge, a position he restated last week while asking the province to halt any work that would preclude switching to that option.

Doerkson has said the Conservatives intend to conduct a review of the tunnel project and its alternatives, though they believe a bridge is the best option.

He said last week that a bridge could save up to $3 billion compared with a tunnel.

The Royal BC Museum is temporarily locking up shop at the BC Archives so that teams can move the delicate items to the new Provincial Archives, Research and Collections (PARC) Campus in Colwood.

Starting Nov. 22, the BC Archives will close to the public to accommodate the move, which involves carefully packing up each item and then unpacking it at the new facility.

Materials will be unavailable to the public until they’re unpacked. The museum plans to open the new reading room at the PARC Campus in spring 2027, before regular service restarts in full in fall 2027.

“Moving to PARC Campus marks an exciting new chapter for the BC Archives,” said Jodi Giesbrecht, vice president of archives, research and collections at the Royal BC Museum.

“PARC Campus will provide a home for irreplaceable records that support research and community knowledge, and safeguard our broader understanding of British Columbia’s past and present,” she said. “We recognize the impact of the temporary closure and look forward to welcoming people into this exceptional new home.”

The museum notes its online BC Archives resources are still available while the physical archives are closed down.

The new PARC Campus is still under construction, with hopes to open in spring 2027. It was originally scheduled to open this year when construction of the $270 million facility kicked off in 2023.

RELATED: Sneak peek inside Royal BC Museum’s new PARC Campus in Colwood

The Colwood facility has been dubbed a “state-of-the-art” research and collections building with space for labs, displays, events, and public access to archives.

Part of the PARC Campus also features glass walls where visitors can see museum researchers work – from cleaning dinosaur fossils to cataloguing insects.

Previously, the museum said the PARC Campus would help the public see more of the Royal BC Museum’s collection, as currently only about one per cent of its collection is ever on display at a time.

The new facility is part of the museum’s two-campus plan, with the downtown site continuing to host the IMAX theatre and major exhibits.

The Homalco First Nation has acquired Tyee Plaza, a shopping complex in downtown Campbell River.

The nation announced it took over the 10-acre waterfront space on Wednesday.

Over the next 12 to 24 months, the Homalco First Nation will be focused on capital planning and working with current tenants and other stakeholders to maintain stability.

In the future, it’s considering further civic partnerships, Indigenous entrepreneurship, and even potential mixed-use development on the property.

“We recognize that Tyee Plaza is an important part of downtown Campbell River. We would like to extend our sincere appreciation to former ownership for their stewardship as we maintain this positive momentum going forward.”

Tyee Plaza, located at 1111 Shoppers Row, includes a range of businesses and tenants, including No Frills, Shoppers Drug Mart, Anytime Fitness, Bulk Barn, Quesada, and Island Health.

“This acquisition is a monumental milestone for Homalco First Nation. “For Homalco, establishing a substantial presence in the heart of Campbell River is a source of tremendous pride. Our people have deep historical and cultural connections to this region, and this investment represents another chapter in our Nation’s journey toward reclaiming our economic strength and building a sustainable future,” he said.

An official ribbon-cutting ceremony to mark the handover to the Homalco First Nation is planned for Saturday, Nov. 28.

The sale price for the shopping plaza has not been disclosed.
